chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants.
But He is a tyrant to the tyrants.

key_terms.الظَّالِمِينَ: The tyrants / those who are unjust to themselves
key_terms.ظَلَّامٌ: A tyrant / one who deals unjustly

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God being unjust to the unjust and being unjust to His servants?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that divine justice (*‘adl*) is not a general attribute applied uniformly but is contingent upon the servant’s own actions, specifically that God is unjust only to those who are unjust to themselves. This aligns with the Shia doctrine of *‘Adl*, emphasizing that punishment is a consequence of self-inflicted spiritual loss rather than arbitrary divine decree. The Imam’s statement underscores the principle that God’s mercy is vast, but His justice manifests precisely where human agency creates imbalance.
